Sus funciones incluyen el mantenimiento general, como lavado a presión, limpieza de ventanas, recolección de basura y tareas de limpieza rutinarias. El portero también apoya en la preparación y limpieza de eventos cuando sea necesario y responde a las inquietudes de limpieza conforme surgen. El puesto requiere responsabilidad, atención al detalle y la capacidad de trabajar de manera profesional y cortés con el personal de la propiedad, los residentes y los visitantes. #WeShowUp Responsabilidades: Garantiza que todas las áreas comunes, incluidos aceras, vestíbulos, baños y espacios públicos, se mantengan limpias y presentables. Completa las tareas diarias de limpieza y mantenimiento según lo asignado por el Gerente Senior de Operaciones, Limpieza. Realiza lavado a presión en las áreas asignadas por la gerencia. Se presenta en la ubicación asignada usando el uniforme aprobado de ParkX Porter. Llega a la ubicación asignada antes del inicio del turno de trabajo. Garantiza el cumplimiento de todas las normas de seguridad y estándares de limpieza. Mantiene una actitud profesional y cortés con todos los visitantes del sitio. Reconoce, saluda e interactúa de manera profesional con el personal de la propiedad y los invitados, siguiendo los protocolos correspondientes. Apoya a los equipos de gestión con solicitudes especiales de limpiez

We're looking for generalists: engineers who can move between these layers, reason from first principles about a system they haven't seen before, and pick the problem that matters most rather than the one closest to their prior experience. Our system changes as fast as the research does, correctness under failure matters as much as throughput, and the best solutions often come from understanding the ML workload well enough to know which guarantees it actually needs. This role sits squarely across research and engineering. You'll develop next-generation architectures and RL algorithms, take them from a small-scale result to a frontier-scale run, and understand every place they behave differently along the way. jobs.title: Staff / Senior Physical Security Systems Engineer
jobs.description_text: About the role Data Center Security Engineering (DCSE) secures Anthropic's data center footprint; this role covers how the sites are designed and built to be secure. Much of that footprint is designed and built with partners, so a site's security is decided early: in what Anthropic hands the people who build it, and in how rigorously the delivered systems are tested against it. You'll design and specify the physical security systems for a site: perimeter and vehicle barriers, intrusion detection, video, security lighting, and the site penetrations and utility entry points that bypass them. Design firms and integrators produce the site drawings and install; you specify, review, and verify. You'll write the performance requirement and verification method behind each control, review every site design against them at each stage with redlines a design team can act on, test in the field that what was built performs as specified, and re-verify post-acceptance changes. This is a foundational role. You'll own Anthropic's physical security reference design package (typical details, reference drawings, schedules, and test procedures) in the form partners build from, and keep it current against each site's threat basis and the sites actually being built. You'll set the technical position for a site and decide what applies where; where a requirement can't be met as written, you'll engineer the compensating control and document the deviation. jobs.description_text: About the role Frontier AI is on track to be among the most consequential and most adversarially-targeted technology in the world. The capability curve is steep, the adversaries who want these systems are extremely well-resourced, and the security bar this will eventually require is well beyond where the industry operates today. Incremental hardening alone is not going to close that gap, so we need breakthroughs and a group of people to go find them. Security Labs is that team. We run a portfolio of high-risk, high-expected-value security projects: the work that seems impractical until someone optimistic and stubborn enough actually tries it. Projects run on the order of weeks rather than quarters, and each one is either handed off to the Anthropic team that will own it in production or wound down with a writeup of what we learned. We expect a meaningful fraction of our bets not to land. This team is intentionally scrappy and ambitious. We're intentionally iterating fast on high-risk research bets and we expect a meaningful fraction not to land. If a 30% project success rate sounds uncomfortable, or uncharted and chaotic territory isn’t both frightening and exciting, this probably isn't the right fit. There are other places in Anthropic Security doing important work with more structure, less risk, and more certain paths to positive outcomes.
